nodes.label: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
nodes.author: Mor Geva, Roei Schuster, Jonathan Berant, Omer Levy

nodes.label: Feed-Forward Layers as Key-Value Memories
nodes.rationale: Feed-forward layers emulate neural key-value memories where keys detect input patterns and values induce output vocabulary distributions; differs from softmax-normalized memory only in activation function.

nodes.label: Keys Capture Input Patterns
nodes.rationale: Each key vector correlates with human-interpretable patterns (shallow n-grams in lower layers, semantic topics in upper layers); 65-80% of trigger examples associate with identified patterns.

nodes.label: Values Represent Output Distributions
nodes.rationale: Value vectors induce distributions over vocabulary; upper-layer values show 3.5% agreement rate with next-token of key trigger examples (vs 0.0004% random baseline).

nodes.label: Memory Aggregation and Refinement
nodes.rationale: Feed-forward layer output composes hundreds of active memories; residual connections refine predictions layer-by-layer, with ~33% of predictions determined in bottom layers.

nodes.label: Layer-Wise Pattern Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Lower layers (1-9) dominated by shallow patterns; upper layers (10-16) by semantic patterns. Removing last token impacts memory coefficient more in lower layers.

edges.rationale: Key vectors in the memory formulation are shown to capture interpretable input patterns through trigger example analysis.
Value vectors in the memory formulation induce distributions over output vocabulary, complementing key patterns.
Pattern analysis reveals hierarchical organization: shallow patterns in lower layers, semantic patterns in upper layers.
Agreement rate between key patterns and value predictions increases in upper layers, indicating layer-dependent semantic alignment.
Memory aggregation describes how individual memory cells compose to form layer output and how residual connections refine predictions across layers.

hyperedges.label: Feed-Forward Layer Interpretation as Memory System
hyperedges.rationale: These four concepts collectively explain the complete mechanism of feed-forward layers: they function as key-value memories where keys detect patterns, values predict outputs, and multiple memories aggregate to form layer predictions.
